PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
TO: Rebecca Thorsen, GC, Vantage Logistics Group. FROM: H&C engagement team (for C. Ng review). RE: Seven-state paid leave matrix and gap analysis (Handbook Rev. 1/15/2022 v. law).
Frame: analysis is framed at the engagement timeline (April-May 2025) using 2025 figures; rates, caps and facility dates move annually, and several milestones have since passed. Status and 2026 figures must be re-confirmed before reliance. Local ordinances and FMLA are out of scope (Engagement Letter 2.4), but flagged where they bite.

BOTTOM LINE
1. The Handbook is one uniform policy built around a narrow, employee-only, 1:40, capped, no-carryover, 120-day sick leave model. It fails NJ, NY and CT sick leave law on accrual, caps, carryover, uses, family definition and documentation, and fails NY and (for new hires) CO/MA/OR/WA on waiting periods or caps.
2. The self-funded PFL benefit (50% AWW, $850, 8 weeks) is not an approved private plan anywhere (Thorsen email 3/12/25: never applied). It cannot substitute for NJ FLI, NY PFL or CT PL and falls below every state. It also does not exist as an option in CO as an unapproved plan.
3. Four registrations are open; CO is probably already late and MA is on the critical path.
4. PinnacleHR's report contains stale or wrong data, and our own memo cannot rely on it.

MATRIX (R = non-compliant, Y = partial/at risk, G = compliant). 2025 figures.
PAID SICK LEAVE
Accrual: statutes NJ, NY, CT, MA, OR, CO 1 hr/30 hrs worked; WA 1/40. Handbook 1/40. NJ R, NY R, CT R, MA R, OR R, CO R, WA G.
Cap/usage: NJ 40; NY 56 (100+ employees); CT 40; MA 40; OR 40 (80 accrual cap); CO 48; WA none. Handbook 40 FT/24 PT. NJ R, NY R, CT R, MA R, OR R, CO R, WA R (part-time cap is unlawful everywhere; Muñoz tracker shows PT employees capped at 24 and one note concedes NJ law requires 40).
Waiting period: NJ 120th day (lawful), CT 120 days (lawful), MA 90, OR 91, WA 90, NY none, CO none. Handbook 120 uniformly. NJ G, CT G, NY R, CO R, MA R, OR R, WA R. Live example: Queens employee Novak (hired 10/15/24) denied leave 1/28/25.
Carryover: NJ, NY, CT, MA, OR, WA require carryover (NJ/CT/MA/OR/WA 40 hrs; NY up to the cap; CO 48) unless the employer frontloads the full amount. Handbook zero carryover, no frontloading. R in all seven; tracker shows forfeitures (NJ 12h, 8h; NY 18h, 14h).
Covered uses: all seven cover family care, preventive care, domestic violence/sexual assault/stalking, public health closures; NJ also school events and bereavement; CO adds bereavement and public-health 80 hrs. Handbook: own illness/appointments only. R in all seven (this is the Muñoz claim).
Family definition: statutes cover domestic partners, siblings, grandparents, grandchildren, in-laws, and (NJ, CO, WA, OR, CT, MA variants) chosen family. Handbook spouse/child/parent. R in all.
Documentation: NJ, NY, CT, WA, OR, MA bar requiring proof before about 3 consecutive days (WA 4 days; CO 4 days); Handbook 2 days, discipline for lateness. R/Y.
Notice/posting: Handbook silent; NJ, NY, CT, MA, CO, OR, WA require posters and written notices. Y.
PAID FAMILY LEAVE (state plans; Vantage benefit is not one)
Benefit: NJ 85%, $1,081, 12 wks; NY 67%, $1,177.32, 12; CT 95%/60% tier, $981, 12 (PINNACLE shows $941, a prior-year number); MA up to 80%, $1,170.64, 12 family (20 medical, 26 combined); CO up to 90%, about $1,324 (verify), 12 (+4); OR to 100% tiered, $1,636.56, 12 (+2); WA 90% tiered, $1,542, 12 (up to 18). Vantage 50%, $850, 8: R in all seven.
Eligibility: states use earnings thresholds, not tenure; none requires 12 months plus 1,000 hours (WA requires 820 hours). Handbook R.
Reasons/family: states include own serious health condition, military exigency, safe leave (varies), broader family. Handbook R.
Notice: 30 days foreseeable only; unforeseeable "as soon as practicable". Handbook flat 30 days; CT incident (10 days' notice) shows practice departing from policy. R/Y.
Job protection: NJ, NY, CT, MA, OR (after 90 days), CO (after 180 days), WA (hours-based, employer size) all provide reinstatement. Handbook ties it to FMLA key-employee rules and 8 weeks. Y/R.
PAID MEDICAL LEAVE
NJ TDI 85%/26 wks; NY DBL $170/wk/26 wks; CT, MA, CO, OR, WA own-condition leave in state plans. Handbook: none; employees directed to employee-paid Keystone STD. Withholding exists for NJ, NY, CT, so benefits exist; the gap is misdirection (7+ inquiries across Bridgeport, Edison, Queens). R for administration; state plans cannot be offset by STD.
EMPLOYER OBLIGATIONS
NJ, NY, CT: registered and remitting; Y because rates are wrong (below). MA, CO, OR, WA: R (no registration, no payroll set-up). MA 2025 rate 0.88% on wages to $176,100; employer 25+ pays 0.42% medical, employee up to 0.46% (Pinnacle shows 0.318%, an error). WA 2025 total 0.92% (employer 28.48% at 50+) versus Pinnacle 0.74%. CO 0.9% split 50/50 (10+ employees). OR 1.0% split 60/40 (25+). Recordkeeping: the manual tracker has no audit trail, tracks only sick leave, and has negative balances (Kowalski -2.5, Ali -0.75). Y/R.
PTO PAYOUT
CO: required; forfeiture is void (Nieto v. Clark's Market, 2021 CO 48). MA: Wage Act treats earned vacation as wages. NJ, NY, OR, WA, CT: payout turns on written policy (CT payout is Vantage policy, not mandatory under C.G.S. 31-76k as the Handbook claims). Handbook R for CO and MA; G for NJ, NY, OR, WA, CT provided forfeiture is clearly written. The 5-day cap with March 31 forfeiture is also R in CO and likely MA (cap accrual, do not forfeit earned time).

GAP ANALYSIS

CRITICAL
C1. NJ/NY/CT sick leave and live exposure (NJ-ESL-2025-04117). Every sick leave term in 6.2 is deficient. DOL reserved a broader audit, and tracker data (rolling forfeitures, undercrediting, PT caps, the 120-day denial in NY) supplies the proof. We also found a misstatement risk: our 2/21/25 response said the policy permits family-member care and defines relatives; Handbook 6.2.5 and 6.2.6 limit use to the employee's own needs. Correct it promptly and consider making Muñoz whole and restoring forfeited hours company-wide. The promised July 1 revision is a commitment to the Department. Penalty and look-back exposure (NJ cites N.J.S.A. 34:11D-7; wage-theft liquidated damages may apply) should be modeled for NJ and NY employees, about 1,570 people.
C2. Colorado. Three remote hires started April 2025. FAMLI and HFWA attach to employees working in Colorado from day one, not from the facility opening; registration and quarterly premiums are likely already due. Pinnacle's note that private plans are unavailable in CO is wrong (FAMLI permits approved private plans), but the self-funded plan would still need equal benefits and approval. Offer letters must carry the payout language Ms. Thorsen directed.
C3. Massachusetts. MA employers must register on MassTaxConnect before the first paycheck. With PinnacleHR needing 6-8 weeks after registration and the August 1 opening (about 60-70 employees in place at opening, recruiting begins May), register no later than the week of May 19; absolute last date is about June 6.
C4. Payroll contribution errors in the three live states. Pinnacle shows NJ FLI 0.09% on $161,400 and TDI employee 0.00%; the 2025 rates are 0.33% FLI and 0.23% TDI on $165,400 (I could not confirm on the NJ DOL site; confirm). If so, withholding and remittance are short by roughly $200,000 or more annually; employer liability for unremitted contributions is likely. Also confirm NY DBL carrier coverage and CT $981 cap.
C5. Misdirecting claims. Instructing employees to use voluntary Keystone STD instead of state plans (NJ TDI, NY DBL, CT PL) creates retroactive claim and retaliation/interference risk. Issue corrective guidance and notices now; audit 12 months of inquiries.

HIGH
H1. Self-funded PFL. It is not an approved private plan in NJ, NY, CT (confirmed: no application). The Handbook statements that it "meets or exceeds" the states and is "intended to satisfy" mandates are false and misleading to employees (CT employees are already asking). Recommended path: participate in all seven state programs, drop the "satisfies the mandate" language, and either retire the 50% benefit or redesign it as a clearly labeled top-up (a cost decision). A private plan route would require equal or better benefits everywhere, so it is not recommended.
H2. Sick leave in expansion states (MA, OR, WA, CO). Redraft by state; WA has no cap; CO 48 hours.
H3. PTO payout in CO and MA; the 5-day carryover/March 31 forfeiture in those states. MA Wage Act exposure includes mandatory treble damages.
H4. PFL eligibility, notice, job protection and anti-retaliation language (see matrix) and missing state notices.
H5. Manual spreadsheet tracking. Errors are documented, state rules are not encoded, and the 50-75% workload increase is not sustainable; recommend leave software (HR estimate $40,000-75,000) within the $175,000 budget alongside legal fees (estimated $28,000-42,000).

MODERATE
M1. Oregon registration by about November 2025 and Washington by about January 2026; facility openings February 1 and May 1, 2026.
M2. Local law outside scope but affecting operations: NYC (Maspeth), Westchester (White Plains), Seattle/Tacoma drivers, Denver and Portland ordinances; confirm in writing whether to add.
M3. Documentation thresholds, posting, written notices, six-year retention versus state minimums.
M4. Vendor communication: share only non-privileged action lists with Pinnacle and Keystone.

REMEDIATION PLAN (owners; dates)
Immediately (this week): Legal/HR: CO FAMLI registration and sick leave accrual for the three hires; MA PFML registration and ESTL policy; written guidance to HR that sick leave is usable per state law (NY: immediately; no 120-day denials); stop the 2-day documentation rule; correct and supplement the DOL response (H&C). Pinnacle (Samuelson): confirm 2025 NJ/CT rates and under-withholding.
By May 30: Restore forfeited sick hours and correct balances; direct STD/PFL claimants to state plans; issue notices.
By July 1: State-specific Handbook (separate engagement; excluded from our scope) with seven state riders; CO and MA payout language; delete self-funded "satisfies" language.
By August 1: MA live (HRIS/ClockSync/Pinnacle configured). October: OR registration; CO live November 1. December-January: WA registration; leave software live Q1 2026; post-launch audit.

UNRESOLVED / VERIFY: current-year rates and facility status; NJ rate confirmation on official site; CO benefit cap; local ordinances; NJ/NY private plan history; whether any Colorado, Massachusetts or other registrations were completed after April 2025.
